Although the original caves cannot be freely visited, the **Risco Caído Interpretation Centre** provides an excellent introduction to the archaeological, cultural and astronomical significance of one of the most extraordinary discoveries in the Canary Islands.

### The Visit
Through interactive exhibitions, reconstructions and audiovisual presentations, the centre explains how the ancient inhabitants of Gran Canaria used sacred caves and observed the cycles of the Sun and Moon to organise their daily lives. It is an essential experience for anyone wishing to understand the island's rich pre-Hispanic heritage.

### Before You Go
- 🎟️ Check opening hours and guided tour availability in advance
- 🎧 The exhibitions include interactive and audiovisual content
- 🏛️ An excellent complement to exploring the mountain landscapes of central Gran Canaria
- 📸 The surrounding scenery offers spectacular viewpoints worth visiting

### Recommendation
Take the opportunity to explore the landscapes of Artenara and the central highlands of Gran Canaria, one of the areas with the greatest cultural and natural significance in the Canary Islands.
pois.shortDescription: UNESCO World Heritage Site showcasing the pre-Hispanic archaeological and astronomical legacy of Risco Caído in Gran Canaria.

pois.name: Basílica de Nuestra Señora del Pino
pois.description:
The **Basilica of Our Lady of the Pine** is the most important religious site in Gran Canaria and one of the leading pilgrimage destinations in the Canary Islands. Located in the historic town of Teror, it houses the image of **Our Lady of the Pine**, the patron saint of Gran Canaria, whose devotion remains a central part of the island's cultural and religious identity.

### The Visit
Its elegant façade, impressive bell tower and valuable collection of religious artwork make the basilica an essential stop for visitors interested in the history and culture of Gran Canaria. Every year, thousands of pilgrims travel to Teror to take part in the Feast of the Pine celebrations, one of the most important religious and cultural events in the Canary Islands.

### Before You Go
- ⛪ Respectful clothing is recommended when entering the basilica
- 📸 The square and historic surroundings offer excellent photography opportunities
- 🏛️ Combine your visit with a walk through the traditional streets of Teror
- 🎉 Visitor numbers are especially high during the Feast of the Pine celebrations

### Recommendation
Explore the historic centre of Teror, admire its famous wooden balconies and enjoy local cuisine in one of the most charming towns in Gran Canaria.
pois.shortDescription: The sanctuary of Our Lady of the Pine, patron saint of Gran Canaria, located in the historic town of Teror.

pois.name: Iglesia de San Juan Bautista de Arucas
pois.description:
The **Church of San Juan Bautista de Arucas** is one of the most impressive landmarks in Gran Canaria and the architectural symbol of the city of Arucas. Popularly known as the **Cathedral of Arucas**, despite not holding cathedral status, it is renowned for its magnificent **Neo-Gothic architecture** and for being built entirely from blue volcanic stone quarried locally.

### The Visit
Its soaring towers, colourful stained-glass windows, intricate stone carvings and majestic interior make this church one of the finest architectural achievements in the Canary Islands. Constructed between the late 19th and early 20th centuries, it reflects the prosperity and ambition that shaped the development of Arucas.

### Before You Go
- 📸 Its façade is one of the most photographed landmarks in Gran Canaria
- ⛪ Respectful clothing is recommended when visiting the church
- 🎟️ Check opening hours and religious service schedules in advance
- 🌅 The volcanic stone is particularly beautiful in the light of sunset

### Recommendation
Take time to explore the historic centre of Arucas, visit its plazas and gardens, and discover the charm of one of the most architecturally remarkable towns in Gran Canaria.
pois.shortDescription: The famous Cathedral of Arucas, a stunning Neo-Gothic church built entirely from blue volcanic stone.

pois.name: Necrópolis de Arteara
pois.description:
The **Arteara Necropolis** is one of the most important archaeological sites in Gran Canaria and the largest pre-Hispanic burial ground on the island. Located in the spectacular Arteara Valley, in the municipality of San Bartolomé de Tirajana, it preserves hundreds of funerary mounds that provide valuable insight into the beliefs, rituals and social organisation of the ancient inhabitants of Gran Canaria.

### The Visit
The archaeological complex stretches across the slopes of the valley, creating a remarkable cultural landscape surrounded by palm groves, ravines and volcanic mountains. With more than 800 funerary structures, it is one of the most significant surviving testimonies of the indigenous heritage of the Canary Islands. Visitors can gain a deeper understanding of ancient burial practices and the spiritual importance this site held for the island's early inhabitants.

### Before You Go
- ☀️ Bring sun protection, as much of the site is exposed to direct sunlight
- 👟 Comfortable footwear is recommended for exploring the surrounding paths
- 📸 The panoramic views of the valley are ideal for landscape photography
- 🏛️ The interpretation centre provides valuable historical and archaeological context

### Recommendation
Take time to explore the Arteara Valley and the surrounding landscapes of Gran Canaria's interior, where nature, history and tradition come together in a unique setting.
pois.shortDescription: The largest indigenous necropolis in Gran Canaria, featuring hundreds of ancient burial mounds in the spectacular Arteara Valley.

pois.name: Museo Castillo de Mata
pois.description:
One of the most important historic fortresses in Gran Canaria and a key site for understanding the development of Las Palmas de Gran Canaria. Built to defend the city from pirate attacks and maritime threats, **Castillo de Mata** combines military history, cultural heritage and local history in the heart of the island's capital.

### The Visit
The museum explores several centuries of urban and maritime history through exhibitions, scale models, historical documents and restored areas of the original fortress. Its galleries illustrate how the city grew around its port and highlight the strategic importance of Gran Canaria along Atlantic trade and navigation routes.

### Before You Go
- ⏳ Allow at least one hour to enjoy the full visit
- 📸 The fortress walls and historic spaces offer excellent photo opportunities
- 🏛️ An ideal addition to a cultural tour of Las Palmas de Gran Canaria
- 🎟️ Check opening hours and temporary exhibitions before visiting

### Recommendation
Continue exploring the historic centre of the city and discover other iconic landmarks that have shaped the history of Las Palmas de Gran Canaria.
pois.shortDescription: Historic fortress transformed into a museum dedicated to the urban and maritime history of Las Palmas de Gran Canaria.

pois.name: Castillo de la Luz
pois.description:
The **Castillo de la Luz** is the oldest fortress in the Canary Islands and one of the most iconic historical landmarks in Las Palmas de Gran Canaria. Built in the 15th century to defend the city and its harbour from pirate attacks, it has witnessed some of the most significant events in the history of Gran Canaria.

### The Visit
Today, the fortress houses a cultural centre dedicated to the renowned Gran Canarian sculptor **Martín Chirino**, combining historic heritage with contemporary art in a unique setting. Its walls, courtyards and exhibition spaces allow visitors to explore centuries of history while enjoying important artistic displays.

### Before You Go
- 🎟️ Check the current temporary exhibitions before your visit
- 📸 The exterior of the fortress offers excellent photo opportunities
- 🏛️ An ideal stop when exploring the harbour area and La Isleta district
- ⏳ Allow at least one hour to fully explore the site

### Recommendation
Take a walk around the harbour surroundings and discover how this historic stronghold helped transform Las Palmas into one of the most important Atlantic cities of its time.
pois.shortDescription: The oldest fortress in the Canary Islands, now a cultural space dedicated to contemporary art and local heritage.

pois.name: Roque Nublo
pois.description:
Rising above the central highlands of the island, **Roque Nublo** is one of the most impressive and recognisable natural landmarks in Gran Canaria. This spectacular volcanic monolith, standing approximately 80 metres high, forms part of a unique mountain landscape that has held great cultural and spiritual significance since the time of the island's ancient inhabitants.

### The Visit
Surrounded by pine forests, deep ravines and volcanic formations, Roque Nublo offers some of the finest panoramic views in Gran Canaria. From its surroundings, visitors can admire the island's mountainous interior and, on clear days, the silhouette of the majestic **Mount Teide** on Tenerife rising above the Atlantic Ocean.

### Before You Go
- 👟 Access requires a short walk along a well-marked trail
- 🧥 Bring a light jacket, especially during the winter months
- 📸 One of the best locations on the island for landscape photography
- 🌅 Sunrise and sunset provide particularly spectacular lighting conditions

### Recommendation
Take a moment to appreciate the silence and the sweeping mountain views. Few places capture the natural essence of Gran Canaria better than this iconic volcanic monument.
pois.shortDescription: Roque Nublo, Gran Canaria's most iconic natural landmark, offers spectacular views of Mount Teide and some of the island's finest mountain scenery.

pois.name: Roque Bentayga
pois.description:
One of the most iconic and sacred landmarks in Gran Canaria, **Roque Bentayga** rises above the spectacular landscapes of Tejeda as a symbol of the island's ancient history and spiritual heritage. This striking volcanic rock formation was an important ceremonial site for the indigenous inhabitants of Gran Canaria and remains one of the most remarkable cultural and natural attractions in the Canary Islands.

### The Visit
At its base, visitors can explore archaeological remains, rock engravings and ancient ceremonial areas that reveal the significance of this site to the island's pre-Hispanic population. The surrounding landscape offers exceptional views of **Roque Nublo**, the central highlands and the deep ravines that define the interior of Gran Canaria.

### Before You Go
- 👟 Easy access suitable for most visitors
- 📸 One of the best locations for photographing the landscapes of Tejeda
- ☀️ Bring sun protection, as there is very little shade
- 🏛️ The interpretation centre provides valuable insight into its historical and cultural importance

### Recommendation
Take time to explore the surrounding area of Tejeda, considered one of the most beautiful villages in Spain and one of the greatest treasures of Gran Canaria's mountain region.
pois.shortDescription: A sacred volcanic rock formation of the ancient Canarians, set within the spectacular mountain landscapes of Tejeda.

pois.name: Parque Natural de Tamadaba
pois.description:
The **Tamadaba Natural Park** protects one of Gran Canaria's greatest natural treasures and forms part of the island's **UNESCO Biosphere Reserve**. This vast protected area is home to some of the best-preserved Canary Island pine forests, deep ravines and an impressive network of cliffs that plunge dramatically into the Atlantic Ocean.

### The Visit
Exploring Tamadaba means immersing yourself in a landscape where nature remains largely untouched. Its mountain roads, forest trails and natural viewpoints provide outstanding panoramas of the northwest coast and the island's central highlands. One of the highlights is the **Llanos de la Mimbre Viewpoint**, where visitors can admire the Atlantic Ocean, rugged coastal cliffs and, on clear days, the silhouette of **Mount Teide** rising above Tenerife.

### Before You Go
- 👟 Trails are available for a wide range of hiking abilities
- 🧥 Temperatures are often cooler than along the coast
- 📸 An exceptional destination for nature photography and scenic views
- 🌲 Respect protected areas and stay on marked paths

### Recommendation
Complete your visit with a trip down to Agaete or Puerto de las Nieves, where you can enjoy fresh seafood while admiring the contrast between Tamadaba's mountains and the Atlantic Ocean.
pois.shortDescription: Gran Canaria's largest Canary pine forest, surrounded by dramatic cliffs, hiking trails and panoramic Atlantic views.

pois.name: Dunas de Maspalomas
pois.description:
The **Maspalomas Dunes** are one of Gran Canaria's most iconic landmarks and one of the most unique natural environments in Europe. This extraordinary sea of golden sand stretches along the Atlantic coastline, creating a remarkable setting where desert landscapes, ocean views and the island's southern sunlight merge into an unforgettable scene.

### The Visit
Protected as a Special Nature Reserve, the area covers more than 400 hectares and includes vast shifting dunes, a palm oasis and the Maspalomas Lagoon, an important refuge for migratory birds. Walking across the rolling sand ridges offers the opportunity to experience one of the Canary Islands' most celebrated landscapes and enjoy unique views of the southern coast.

### Before You Go
- ☀️ Bring water, sun protection and a hat
- 👟 The sand can become extremely hot during the summer months
- 📸 Sunrise and sunset provide the best conditions for photography
- 🌿 Respect protected areas and remain on designated paths

### Recommendation
Complete your visit with a walk along Maspalomas Beach or watch the sunset beside the historic Maspalomas Lighthouse, one of the most recognisable landmarks in Gran Canaria.
pois.shortDescription: The Maspalomas Dunes form a spectacular sea of sand beside the Atlantic Ocean and one of the most iconic landscapes in the Canary Islands.

pois.name: Caldera de Bandama
pois.description:
The **Bandama Caldera** is one of the most impressive reminders of Gran Canaria's volcanic origins. Located just a few kilometres from Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, this विशाल natural depression, formed by a volcanic eruption thousands of years ago, measures nearly one kilometre in diameter and more than 200 metres deep, making it one of the best-preserved volcanic craters in the Canary Islands.

### The Visit
From the nearby **Bandama Peak**, visitors can enjoy one of the finest panoramic views in northeastern Gran Canaria, overlooking the crater, the coastline and the island's inland mountains. At the bottom of the caldera, historic vineyards and agricultural plots still survive, creating a remarkable contrast between volcanic landscapes and centuries of human activity.

### Before You Go
- 📸 The Bandama Peak viewpoint offers the best overall views of the caldera
- 👟 Wear comfortable footwear if you plan to walk along the rim or descend into the crater
- ☀️ Sun protection is recommended throughout the year
- 🌅 Sunrise and sunset provide the most striking light for appreciating the colours and textures of the volcanic landscape

### Recommendation
Complete your visit by exploring the surrounding vineyards and wineries, one of the most traditional wine-producing areas of Gran Canaria.
pois.shortDescription: The Bandama Caldera is one of the best-preserved volcanic craters in the Canary Islands, offering panoramic views and remarkable geological heritage.

pois.name: Mirador del Balcón
pois.description:
Perched above the dramatic cliffs of Gran Canaria's western coastline, the **Balcón Viewpoint** offers one of the most breathtaking panoramas in the Canary Islands. From this platform overlooking the Atlantic Ocean, visitors can admire the famous **Dragon's Tail**, a striking sequence of mountain ridges whose silhouette resembles the spine of a giant dragon stretching into the sea.

### The Visit
The combination of towering cliffs, endless ocean views and largely untouched landscapes makes this one of the finest places to experience the wild side of Gran Canaria. Its privileged location provides outstanding views of the island's remote western coast, one of the most spectacular and least developed regions of the archipelago.

### Before You Go
- 📸 One of the best viewpoints in Gran Canaria for landscape photography
- 🌅 Sunset provides particularly spectacular lighting across the cliffs
- 🌬️ Winds can be strong, especially during the winter months
- 🚗 Parking is available next to the viewpoint

### Recommendation
Continue along the scenic route between Agaete and La Aldea de San Nicolás to discover deep ravines, dramatic cliffs and some of the most impressive and unspoilt landscapes in Gran Canaria.
pois.shortDescription: Balcón Viewpoint offers the best views of the famous Dragon's Tail formation and the dramatic cliffs of western Gran Canaria.

pois.name: Mirador de Unamuno
pois.description:
Located in the mountainous heart of Gran Canaria, the **Unamuno Viewpoint** offers one of the island's most breathtaking panoramas. From this natural balcony, visitors can enjoy outstanding views of the **Tejeda Caldera**, **Roque Nublo** and **Roque Bentayga**, three of the most iconic geological landmarks in the Canary Islands.

### The Visit
The viewpoint is named after the writer and philosopher **Miguel de Unamuno**, who was deeply inspired by the beauty and grandeur of these mountains during his visit to Gran Canaria. From here, visitors can fully appreciate the scale of the island's ravines, volcanic formations and dramatic landscapes that make the interior of Gran Canaria so unique.

### Before You Go
- 📸 One of the best viewpoints in Gran Canaria for mountain scenery
- 🌅 Sunrise and sunset provide exceptional photography opportunities
- 🧥 Temperatures are usually cooler than on the coast
- 🚗 Easily accessible from the road connecting Tejeda with the central highlands

### Recommendation
Combine your visit with a tour of Tejeda and nearby viewpoints to discover some of the most iconic and photographed landscapes in Gran Canaria.
pois.shortDescription: Unamuno Viewpoint offers spectacular views of the Tejeda Caldera, Roque Nublo and Roque Bentayga in the heart of Gran Canaria.

pois.name: Mirador Degollada de las Yeguas
pois.description:
The **Degollada de las Yeguas Viewpoint** offers one of the most remarkable panoramas in Gran Canaria. Located between the island's central highlands and the southern coast, it overlooks the vast **Tirajana Ravine**, an extraordinary landscape shaped over millions of years by erosion and volcanic activity. Due to its scale and dramatic relief, many visitors compare it to a miniature Grand Canyon.

### The Visit
From this natural balcony, visitors can admire a landscape dominated by deep ravines, steep slopes and striking rock formations that reveal the island's fascinating geological history. The contrast between the ochre-coloured cliffs, the vegetation of the valley and the changing light throughout the day creates an ever-changing and unforgettable view.

### Before You Go
- 📸 One of the best viewpoints in Gran Canaria for panoramic photography
- 🌅 Sunrise and sunset provide particularly spectacular lighting conditions
- 🌬️ Winds can be strong in exposed areas
- 🚗 Easily accessible from the road connecting the central highlands with Maspalomas

### Recommendation
Take a moment to appreciate the scale of the ravine before continuing your journey towards the mountains or the southern coast. It is one of the best places to understand the natural forces that shaped Gran Canaria.
pois.shortDescription: Degollada de las Yeguas Viewpoint offers breathtaking views over the Tirajana Ravine and some of Gran Canaria's most dramatic landscapes.

pois.name: Mirador de Pico de las Nieves
pois.description:
At nearly **2,000 metres above sea level**, the **Pico de las Nieves Viewpoint** stands among the highest points in Gran Canaria and offers an exceptional perspective over the island's mountainous interior. From this remarkable vantage point, visitors can admire a landscape shaped by deep ravines, extensive pine forests and volcanic formations that reveal millions of years of geological history.

### The Visit
The viewpoint overlooks some of Gran Canaria's most iconic landmarks, including **Roque Nublo**, **Roque Bentayga** and the island's central highlands. On clear days, the silhouette of **Mount Teide** on neighbouring Tenerife rises above the Atlantic horizon, creating one of the most memorable panoramas in the Canary Islands.

### Before You Go
- 📸 One of the best viewpoints in the Canary Islands for landscape photography
- 🌅 Sunrise and sunset provide exceptional viewing conditions
- 🧥 Bring warm clothing, as temperatures can be significantly cooler than on the coast
- 🌬️ Strong winds are common, even on sunny days

### Recommendation
Explore the scenic roads and hiking trails of the highlands to discover the diverse landscapes that make this area one of Gran Canaria's greatest natural treasures.
pois.shortDescription: Pico de las Nieves Viewpoint offers spectacular views of Roque Nublo, Mount Teide and the mountainous heart of Gran Canaria.

pois.name: Mirador de Cruz de Tejeda
pois.description:
El **Mirador de Cruz de Tejeda** es uno de los lugares más emblemáticos de las cumbres de Gran Canaria y una parada imprescindible para comprender la espectacular geografía de la isla. Situado en un histórico cruce de caminos utilizado durante siglos por viajeros y comerciantes, ofrece una de las panorámicas más amplias y reconocibles del interior grancanario.

### La visita
Desde este privilegiado balcón natural se contemplan profundos barrancos, extensas laderas volcánicas y algunos de los grandes símbolos de la isla, como el **Roque Nublo** y el **Roque Bentayga**. En los días de mayor visibilidad, la silueta del **Teide** aparece sobre el Atlántico, completando una de las vistas más icónicas de Canarias.

### Antes de ir
- 📸 Uno de los mejores miradores para fotografiar las cumbres de Gran Canaria
- 🌅 El amanecer y el atardecer ofrecen una luz especialmente espectacular
- 🧥 Lleva algo de abrigo, ya que las temperaturas suelen ser más frescas que en la costa
- 🛍️ En los alrededores encontrarás puestos de artesanía y productos típicos canarios

### Recomendación
Dedica tiempo a recorrer los senderos cercanos o a visitar los pueblos de Tejeda y Artenara, dos de los rincones con más encanto y tradición de las montañas de Gran Canaria.
pois.shortDescription: Mirador de Cruz de Tejeda, uno de los balcones naturales más famosos de Gran Canaria, con vistas al Roque Nublo, al Teide y a las cumbres de la isla.

pois.name: Parque Rural de Doramas
pois.description:
The **Doramas Rural Park** protects one of the most valuable and distinctive natural environments in Gran Canaria. Located in the island's northern midlands, it preserves some of the last remnants of the ancient **laurel forest**, the subtropical woodland that once covered much of the Canary Islands before the arrival of the first settlers. Its ecological importance makes it one of the best places to experience the rich biodiversity of Gran Canaria.

### The Visit
This extensive protected area is home to lush ravines, natural springs, humid forests and iconic sites such as **Los Tilos de Moya**. Its trails wind through landscapes dominated by laurels, lindens, ferns and other native species, offering a completely different experience from the island's better-known volcanic and coastal scenery.

### Before You Go
- 👟 Trails are available for a variety of hiking abilities
- 🌿 Stay on marked paths to help protect the ecosystem
- 📸 An excellent destination for nature photography and birdwatching
- 🌧️ Some sections may be damp or slippery after rainfall

### Recommendation
Combine your visit with the villages and viewpoints of northern Gran Canaria to discover one of the greenest, most peaceful and surprising areas of the island.
pois.shortDescription: Doramas Rural Park preserves the last remnants of Gran Canaria's laurel forests and is one of the island's most biodiverse natural areas.

pois.name: Los Azulejos de Veneguera
pois.description:
**Los Azulejos de Veneguera** form one of the island's most remarkable and distinctive geological landscapes. Its striking shades of green, yellow, red and ochre create a vast multicoloured mountainside that contrasts dramatically with the surrounding volcanic terrain, making it one of the most unusual natural wonders in the Canary Islands.

### The Visit
These formations owe their appearance to ancient volcanic and hydrothermal processes that altered the mineral composition of the rocks over millions of years. The result is a natural mosaic of colours and textures that has made this corner of Veneguera a must-see destination for photographers, geology enthusiasts and anyone interested in unique landscapes.

### Before You Go
- 📸 One of the most photogenic locations in Gran Canaria
- ☀️ Bring sun protection, as there is very little shade
- 🚗 Easily visible from the GC-200 scenic road
- 🌅 Early morning and late afternoon light enhance the mountain's colours

### Recommendation
Combine your visit with a drive along the spectacular western coastal road, where deep ravines, Atlantic cliffs and some of Gran Canaria's wildest and least explored landscapes await.
pois.shortDescription: Los Azulejos de Veneguera is a striking multicoloured geological formation shaped by ancient volcanic processes on Gran Canaria's western coast.

pois.name: Barranco de las Vacas
pois.description:
Hidden in the interior of Gran Canaria, the **Barranco de las Vacas** is home to one of the island's most remarkable geological formations. Over thousands of years, water erosion has sculpted a narrow canyon of smooth curves and undulating walls that resembles the famous slot canyons of the American Southwest, making it one of the most photographed locations in Gran Canaria.

### The Visit
Although relatively small in size, the beauty of its shapes and the texture of the rock create a truly unique setting. Golden tones, winding walls and the ever-changing play of light inside the canyon offer a visual experience unlike any other landscape on the island.

### Before You Go
- 📸 Visit early in the day for the best lighting conditions and fewer visitors
- 👟 Wear comfortable footwear suitable for uneven terrain
- ☀️ There is very little shade, especially during the warmer months
- ⚠️ Respect the environment and avoid climbing on the rock formations

### Recommendation
Combine your visit with other locations in the interior of Gran Canaria to discover how erosion and the island's volcanic origins have created landscapes as unique as this remarkable natural canyon.
pois.shortDescription: Barranco de las Vacas is a spectacular canyon of sculpted rock formations and one of the most photographed natural attractions in Gran Canaria.
